title: Construct 3D model from defocus image
aim: To recover the depth, and hence the shape, of a scene from the defocus blur in images taken at different focus settings, and to build a textured 3D surface from the recovered depth map.
objectives: To understand how defocus blur encodes the distance from the plane of focus.
To implement shape from focus with the SML and variance-of-Laplacian measures and sub-slice interpolation.
To build an all-in-focus image and a textured 3D surface, and to try two-image depth from defocus.
theory: A thin lens focuses a point at distance $u$ onto the sensor at distance $v$ when $1/u + 1/v = 1/F$. Points at other distances form a Gaussian blur whose $\sigma$ grows with the distance from the focus plane, so blur carries depth.

Shape from focus captures a focal stack of $N$ images at different focus settings. A focus measure such as the Sum-Modified-Laplacian (SML) or the variance of the Laplacian scores the local sharpness in every slice. The slice with the largest response gives each pixel's depth; a parabola fitted to the log of the three values around the peak refines it to a fraction of a slice. Copying each pixel from its sharpest slice gives an all-in-focus image. Depth from defocus needs only two images, because the ratio of their high-frequency energies depends on the relative blur.
$$\text{SML}(x, y) = \sum_{(i, j) \in W} \left( \left| 2 I(i, j) - I(i - 1, j) - I(i + 1, j) \right| + \left| 2 I(i, j) - I(i, j - 1) - I(i, j + 1) \right| \right)$$
tools: Python 3.11, OpenCV 5.0 (GaussianBlur, filter2D, Laplacian, boxFilter, medianBlur), NumPy, Matplotlib (mplot3d)
dataset: Synthetic focal stack of 15 slices (256 x 256 px) rendered from a PlantVillage tomato leaf image (class Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot) with a known ground-truth depth map.
algorithm: Load the leaf image, resize it to $256 \times 256$ and define a ground-truth depth (a tilted plane plus a Gaussian hill).
Render 15 slices by blurring each pixel with $\sigma = 0.7\,|d - k|$ and adding sensor noise.
Compute the SML and variance-of-Laplacian focus measures of every slice in $7 \times 7$ windows.
Take the slice of maximum response per pixel, refine it by log-parabolic interpolation, median filter and compare with the truth.
Build the all-in-focus image from the sharpest slice of every pixel.
Form the two-image ratio $E_0 / (E_0 + E_{14})$ of Laplacian energies and correlate it with the true depth.
Plot the stack, the focus curves, the depth and error maps, the textured 3D surface and the defocus ratio.

figures.caption: Figure 7.1: Five slices of the synthetic focal stack (focus at 0, 3, 7, 10 and 14) and the ground-truth depth map.
Figure 7.2: Normalised SML focus curves of three pixels. Dashed lines mark the true depth, dotted lines the interpolated estimate.
Figure 7.3: Ground-truth depth, the depths recovered with SML and with the variance of the Laplacian, absolute error maps and error histogram.
Figure 7.4: Ground-truth surface (left) and the recovered surface textured with the all-in-focus composite (right).
Figure 7.5: A single slice against the all-in-focus composite, the two-image blur ratio and its relation to true depth (correlation -0.84).

results: SML recovered the depth with an RMSE of 0.349 and an MAE of 0.071 slices (99.8 % of the pixels within one slice). The variance of the Laplacian did better: RMSE 0.066 and MAE 0.050 slices, with every pixel within one slice.
The focus curves of three sample pixels peak at true depths of 2.42, 11.71 and 8.38 slices. The interpolated estimates were 2.37, 11.76 and 8.32 slices.
The all-in-focus composite has 3.38 times the mean SML of the middle slice. The two-image blur ratio correlates with the true depth with a coefficient of -0.838.
conclusion: The position of maximum sharpness in a focal stack gives the depth of every textured pixel to a fraction of a slice, and together with the all-in-focus image it yields a textured 3D surface. The two-image defocus variant needs far fewer images but is less accurate.
